\section[\texorpdfstring{\pa{ਖ਼ਰਾਬ} (kharāb)}{ਖ਼ਰਾਬ (kharāb)}]{\pa{ਖ਼ਰਾਬ} (kharāb) — faulty; spoilt}

\label{lesson:PA-C279-kharab}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Punjabi for a packet, then the Punjabi for to add up.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \pa{ਖ਼ਰਾਬ}}
\textbf{\pa{ਖ਼ਰਾਬ}} — \emph{kharāb} — \textquotedblleft{}faulty; spoilt\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\pa{ਮੇਰਾ} \pa{ਨਵਾਂ} \pa{ਫ਼ੋਨ} \pa{ਖ਼ਰਾਬ} \pa{ਹੈ।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{merā navāṁ fon kharāb hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My new phone is faulty.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\pa{ਖ਼ਰਾਬ}} (\emph{kharāb}) is a loan, usually traced through Persian to Arabic \emph{kharāb}, \textquotedblleft{}ruin\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kharāb}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{merā navāṁ fon kharāb hai.} — My new phone is faulty.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Punjabi for a packet, then the Punjabi for to add up, then say \emph{kharāb} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\pa{ਨਕਲੀ} (naklī)}{ਨਕਲੀ (naklī)}]{\pa{ਨਕਲੀ} (naklī) — fake; imitation}

Before the new one: say the Punjabi for to add up, then the Punjabi for faulty.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\pa{ਵਟਾਉਣਾ} (vaṭāuṇā)}{ਵਟਾਉਣਾ (vaṭāuṇā)}]{\pa{ਵਟਾਉਣਾ} (vaṭāuṇā) — to exchange; to swap}

\label{lesson:PA-C279-vatauna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Punjabi for fake, then the Punjabi for genuine.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \pa{ਵਟਾਉਣਾ}}
\textbf{\pa{ਵਟਾਉਣਾ}} — \emph{vaṭāuṇā} — \textquotedblleft{}to exchange; to swap\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\pa{ਮੈਂ} \pa{ਖ਼ਰਾਬ} \pa{ਫ਼ੋਨ} \pa{ਕੱਲ੍ਹ} \pa{ਵਟਾਵਾਂਗਾ।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{maiṁ kharāb fon kall vaṭāvāṅgā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I will exchange the faulty phone tomorrow.
\end{quote}

Past (I …): \pa{ਮੈਂ} \pa{ਜੁੱਤੀ} \pa{ਵਟਾਈ}, \emph{maiṁ juttī vaṭāī}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\pa{ਵਟਾਉਣਾ}} (\emph{vaṭāuṇā}) is inherited from Sanskrit \emph{vartayati}, \textquotedblleft{}causes to turn\textquotedblright{}; CDIAL lists Punjabi \emph{baṭāuṇā}, \textquotedblleft{}to cause to be twisted, change\textquotedblright{}, under it (CDIAL 11356).
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\pa{ਸ਼ਿਕਾਇਤ} (shikāit)}{ਸ਼ਿਕਾਇਤ (shikāit)}]{\pa{ਸ਼ਿਕਾਇਤ} (shikāit) — a complaint}

\label{lesson:PA-C279-shikait}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Punjabi for genuine, then the Punjabi for to exchange.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \pa{ਸ਼ਿਕਾਇਤ}}
\textbf{\pa{ਸ਼ਿਕਾਇਤ}} — \emph{shikāit} — \textquotedblleft{}a complaint\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\pa{ਮੈਂ} \pa{ਨਕਲੀ} \pa{ਚੀਜ਼} \pa{ਬਾਰੇ} \pa{ਸ਼ਿਕਾਇਤ} \pa{ਕਰਾਂਗਾ।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{maiṁ naklī chīz bāre shikāit karāṅgā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I will make a complaint about the fake item.
\end{quote}

A feminine noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\pa{ਸ਼ਿਕਾਇਤ}} (\emph{shikāit}) is a loan, usually traced through Persian to Arabic \emph{shikāya}, \textquotedblleft{}a complaint\textquotedblright{}.
